newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares boosted by firm Dow, dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: German shares boosted by firm Dow, dollar strength.

text.p: German shares got off to a firm start on Wednesday, boosted by a recovery in the U.S. markets after U.S. interest rates were kept on hold, and supported by a firmer dollar.
The DAX index of 30 top German shares was up 9.68 points, or 0.34 percent, at 2,824.81 points by 1001 GMT.
Dealers said news of weaker-than-expected November German M3 money supply growth of eight percent released in the morning was also supportive for the market.
"The number was weaker than expected and that should be good for Bunds and the dollar and also positive for stocks," said one dealer.
Traders said that in general the market was relatively quiet. "The market is very calm with lots of people having already closed their books for the end of the year," said one.

After the M3 data the dollar pulled above 1.55 marks, giving a boost to export-oriented German stocks, in particular in the chemicals sector. Shares in chemicals groups Bayer AG and BASF AG were both firmly ahead.

Meanwhile, shares in Germany's third largest bank Commerzbank were the most heavily traded in morning dealings, rising over two percent, or 88 pfennigs to a new year-high of 39.55 marks. The stock had also risen strongly on Tuesday on renewed banking sector merger talk.
"It's the good old takeover story," said one trader.
But dealers said there was no particular story boosting the stock and on Tuesday, the bank said it had no comment on such rumours.

Business software group SAP AG was at the centre of attention after one of its founding members, Hans-Werner Hector, resigned from the supervisory board over differences with the company's chief executive.

The news had pressured the stock on Tuesday but on Wednesday SAP preference shares recovered two marks to trade up at 209 marks. "The market thinks it is better that Hector has gone, even if there has been a bit of mud-slinging," said one dealer.

One of the morning's biggest gainers were shares in pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe, encouraged by news that the company planned to pay a 1996 dividend of one mark per share plus a special payout of 30 pfennigs per share. Gehe shares were up 3.4 percent, or 3.20 marks, at 97.45 marks.
